stories.headline: Iran targets a US base in Bahrain for the second time in three days
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it sent six drones at the radar of a US air defense site at Bahrain's Riffa base on Sunday, its second attack on Bahrain in three days. Bahrain said it intercepted several aerial attacks before they reached their targets, and Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned the strike. Iran repeated that a path to ending its conflict with the US is still open, while a US aircraft carrier arrived in the region.
stories.why_it_matters: Renewed strikes on a Gulf state that hosts US forces raise the risk to American troops and to oil and fuel supplies, and they come as US-Iran peace talks appear stalled.
stories.background: The United States and Israel have been at war with Iran since early 2026, and Iran has repeatedly fired drones and missiles at US bases in Gulf countries. Bahrain, a small island state across the Gulf from Iran, hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet and US air defense sites. After a lull of roughly two months, the US carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm island in recent weeks, and Iran describes its new attacks as retaliation. Washington and Tehran have been holding peace talks that have not produced a deal.

facts.text: Iran attacked Bahrain on Sunday for the second time in three days, ending a lull of about two months.
The Revolutionary Guard said it launched six drones at the radar of a US air defense site at the Riffa base.
Bahrain said it intercepted several aerial attacks before they hit their targets.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt issued statements condemning the attack, carried by Bahrain's state news agency.
Iran said it was retaliating against the US; the attacks follow minor US strikes on Iran's Qeshm island in recent weeks.
Iran reiterated that a path to ending its conflict with the US remains open.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier arrived in the US Central Command area on Sunday, Bloomberg reported, citing an Axios reporter's post that quoted a US official.

Iran says it struck the base.

stories.headline: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge in its largest drone barrage of the war
stories.summary: Ukraine launched more than 1,300 drones at Russia overnight, aiming toward Moscow and hitting the bridge that links Russia to occupied Crimea. The Kremlin called the damage minor, while Crimea's Russian-installed governor said traffic over the bridge was limited. The strike came a day after President Zelenskyy said US-controlled limits on Starshield satellite terminals were letting Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid get through.
stories.why_it_matters: The war is escalating on both sides heading into winter, when Russian strikes on Ukraine's power and rail networks hit civilians hardest; the attack also lands days before Trump meets Putin and Xi.
stories.background: Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and built the Kerch Strait bridge to connect it to Russian territory; Ukraine has struck it before because it is a key supply route. Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and both sides now rely heavily on long-range drones. Ukraine uses SpaceX's Starlink and its military version, Starshield, to guide drones, including interceptor drones that shoot down Russian attack drones. Kyiv has said for weeks that speed limits on those terminals stop its fast interceptors from working. US-brokered peace talks recently ended without a breakthrough.

facts.text: Ukraine fired 1,336 drones at Russia overnight, aiming toward Moscow and striking the bridge linking Russia and Crimea.
Russia's defense ministry said it intercepted or destroyed more drones in 24 hours than at any time since the war began.
The Kremlin said the damage to the bridge was minor.
Crimea's Russian-backed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, said the strike limited traffic over the bridge.
Bloomberg reported the barrage likely also hit an oil refinery and came after US-brokered peace talks ended without a breakthrough.
The Kyiv Independent reported Moscow Oblast was among the main targets and that a fuel depot in Azov, Russia, was reportedly on fire after drone attacks.
Zelenskyy said Russia struck energy and railway infrastructure in eight regions on Saturday night and that many strikes got through because of limits on Starshield terminals.
Zelenskyy said in October that Starlink speed restrictions had hindered the interception of jet-powered Shahed drones, and that about 2,000 Bars interceptor drones were grounded by the caps.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called Russia's demands in the peace talks 'absurd' and said a ceasefire must come first.

stories.headline: China confirms the first Xi-Trump-Putin summit, set for Thursday in Shenzhen
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry confirmed that Xi Jinping will host Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, Nov. 19, the first meeting of the three leaders. Beijing gave no agenda but said the meeting has 'groundbreaking significance'. US officials have pointed to the war in Ukraine, the Middle East and nuclear arms control as likely topics.
stories.why_it_matters: The leaders of the three largest military powers will discuss wars that drive energy prices and nuclear risk. In the day's feed the story was covered by center and left-leaning outlets only.
stories.background: The meeting is planned around the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen this week. Earlier in November Beijing said only that it was in talks about a possible three-way meeting. The US is at war with Iran, a partner of both China and Russia, and is trying to broker an end to Russia's war in Ukraine. Trump is also locked in trade disputes with China and others.

facts.text: China confirmed Xi will hold a trilateral summit with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, Nov. 19.
Beijing did not say what topics the leaders would discuss.
China said the meeting has 'groundbreaking significance'.
US officials have indicated the agenda includes the war in Ukraine, the Middle East situation including global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control, The Hindu reported.
CNBC reported the talks are expected to cover nuclear non-proliferation, the Middle East war, trade and possibly Ukraine.
Earlier in November, China said it was in talks on a possible meeting of the three leaders at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
Trump is set to embark on an Asia trip that The Guardian describes as a foreign-policy push before the end of his term.

stories.headline: Houthis close to within 60 km of Aden as Yemen's government pulls back from key strait
stories.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed government said it was withdrawing its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden, the seat of the internationally recognized government. Military and government sources said Iran-backed Houthi forces had advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the city. Analysts quoted by The New York Times said momentum in the civil war was shifting toward the Houthis.
stories.why_it_matters: Bab el-Mandeb is a chokepoint for shipping between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, so Houthi control can disrupt trade and raise shipping and fuel costs. In the day's feed only center and left-leaning outlets covered it.
stories.background: Yemen's civil war pits the Houthi movement, backed by Iran and in control of the capital Sanaa, against a government backed by Saudi Arabia that operates from the southern port of Aden. Since September the Houthis have seized much of the Red Sea coast near the strait. The fighting is tied to the wider regional war that the US and Israel launched against Iran in February, and the Houthis have also attacked Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping.

facts.text: The government said it was pulling its last forces back from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden.
Houthi forces advanced to within about 60 km of Aden, according to military and government sources cited by AFP.
Forces aligned with the government and Saudi Arabia were moving to strengthen control of Aden.
The retreat leaves the strait under Houthi control; analysts told The New York Times momentum was tilting toward the Houthis.
Houthi gains and attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have strengthened Iran's position in the wider regional conflict, The Hindu reported.
In early November, sources told Al-Monitor the Houthis were within 80 km of Aden.
The Houthis took control of much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a key shipping route in September.

stories.headline: Estonia will close all border crossings with Russia after an attempted attack on a drone maker
stories.summary: Estonia said it will shut every border crossing with Russia from Dec. 1 after an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which officials said was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence. Eight people were detained. The Kremlin denied any involvement, calling the accusation baseless.
stories.why_it_matters: A NATO member sealing its land border with Russia marks a sharp rise in tension on the alliance's eastern edge, and it shows how sabotage attacks on European defense firms are spreading.
stories.background: Estonia, a Baltic state of about 1.3 million people, borders Russia and has been one of Ukraine's strongest backers since Russia's 2022 invasion. Over the past year it has accused Russian intelligence of sabotage on its soil, including an arson attack on another defense company, Milrem Robotics, in the summer. It had already reduced hours at its border crossings and considered closing them. Threod Systems builds reconnaissance and attack drones.

facts.text: Estonia's foreign minister said all border crossing points with Russia will close from Dec. 1.
The decision follows an attempted attack on drone maker Threod Systems in the early hours of Nov. 14.
Estonian authorities detained eight people overnight and said the attempted arson was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence.
Estonia's prime minister linked the attack to Tallinn's support for Ukraine.
Estonia says closing the crossings will help curb hostile activity and sanctions evasion.
The Kremlin denied Russia was behind the attempted arson.

stories.headline: Huge crowd rallies in Prague against government plan for public broadcasters
stories.summary: A very large crowd gathered in Prague's Letná Park on Sunday to oppose Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plan to replace license fees for Czech Television and Czech Radio with direct state funding. Most reports put turnout in the hundreds of thousands, and organizers said it beat a March protest of more than 200,000. Critics say the change would threaten the broadcasters' independence.
stories.why_it_matters: How public media are paid for decides how easily a government can squeeze them, and Czech voters are pushing back on a pattern seen elsewhere in central Europe.
stories.background: Babiš, a billionaire, returned as prime minister at the head of a nationalist-leaning coalition. His government wants to scrap the fees households pay for public TV and radio and fund the broadcasters from the state budget instead. Opponents, including the broadcasters' staff, see this as a way to gain leverage over newsrooms, and the plan has drawn repeated protests this year, including rallies in Prague's Old Town Square in October. Letná Park is where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution that ended communist rule.

facts.text: Hundreds of thousands of people rallied in Prague on Sunday against the government's public-media funding plan.
The plan would replace public media fees with direct state funding for Czech TV and Czech Radio.

stories.headline: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
stories.summary: Spain's maritime rescue service said nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands by boat over the weekend, mostly from West Africa, continuing a surge that led to a migration emergency declaration earlier in the week. Islands officials say they are struggling to cope. Separately, five EU countries were expected on Monday to announce a deportation center for rejected asylum seekers in Rwanda.
stories.why_it_matters: The Atlantic route to the Canaries is one of the world's deadliest, and the surge is feeding Europe's push toward tougher measures such as sending failed asylum seekers to centers outside the EU.
stories.background: The Canary Islands are Spanish territory off northwest Africa, and people from Senegal, Gambia, Guinea and nearby countries try to reach them in overcrowded wooden boats. Arrivals rose sharply in early November, especially on the small island of El Hierro, which declared an emergency. Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta also recently faced a migration crisis. The EU tightened its migration rules in late 2025, opening the way for 'return hubs' outside the bloc.

facts.text: Nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands by boat over two days, Spain's coastguard said Sunday.
Most of those who arrived on Saturday came from Senegal, Gambia and Guinea.
Spanish authorities declared a migration emergency in the archipelago earlier in the week.
El Hierro declared an emergency on Nov. 7 amid the influx.
Brussels Signal reported that arrivals in the Canaries this year have already passed the total for all of last year.
The surge follows a recent migration crisis in Spain's enclave of Ceuta.
Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands were expected on Monday to announce a 'return hub' in Rwanda for failed asylum seekers, the first such facility outside the EU.

stories.headline: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada could work with Chinese carmakers if negotiations with President Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. He said any Chinese investment would have to bring real manufacturing to Canada, not just assembly of imported parts. A day earlier he said he was making progress with Trump on a trade deal.
stories.why_it_matters: Canada's auto plants are tied into US supply chains, so a turn toward China would affect car prices and jobs on both sides of the border. In the day's feed only center and left-leaning outlets covered it.
stories.background: The US and Canada have been in a months-long tariff fight since Trump imposed duties on Canadian goods, including cars and parts. North American carmaking is deeply integrated, with parts crossing the border many times. Carney, a former central banker who became prime minister in 2025, has sought new trade ties in Europe and Asia. He is in Asia for regional summits, including APEC in China, where Xi, Putin and Trump are also due.

facts.text: Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade talks with Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.
He said any Chinese investment would need substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than assembling imported parts.
Asked whether Chinese investment was leverage in the US talks, Carney said Canada would move forward either way.
On Saturday in Manila, Carney said he was 'making progress' with Trump and had spoken with him about a possible trade deal.
Carney is set to share summit stages in China with Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Trump, The New York Times reported.
